correct_recommendations: Fix the scheduler so that a schedule fires once per local wall-clock slot, for example dedupe on the local date and time instead of a 60-second gap, and refund the duplicate charges after support's manual refunds are identified.

Make charge_renewals idempotent per subscription and renewal period, for example skip a subscription that already has a renewal_charges row for that date or send a Payrail idempotency key built from subscription id and renews_on, together with the scheduler fix for send_dunning, and refund the duplicates after the manual refunds are identified.
invalid_options: Change nothing, or only refund the 212 customers.
Move only charge_renewals to 03:30 and leave the scheduler unchanged, because send_dunning still fires twice.
Refund all 212 duplicate charges at once without checking which ones support already refunded by hand.
Treat the duplicate as a Payrail fault.
root_cause: On 25 October, when summer time ended in Europe/Berlin, the local time 02:30 occurred twice, at 00:30 UTC and 01:30 UTC. due_jobs blocks a second firing only within 60 seconds, so charge_renewals fired twice. renews_on advances only in settle_renewals at 05:00, and psp.charge sends no idempotency key, so the second run charged the same 212 subscriptions again. send_dunning fired twice as well.

dependent_facts.true_value: charge_renewals fired at 00:30Z and 01:30Z, both local 02:30, each charging 212
due_jobs skips a job only when the last firing is less than 60 seconds ago
only in settle_renewals, scheduled 05:00 local, so the second run at 01:30Z selected the same subscriptions
also fired twice, 41 emails each time
unknown which of the 212 customers support already refunded by hand; no list exists
dependent_facts.source: none; tickets/KB-519.md states that nobody kept a list

required_questions.question: Why did it fire twice?
required_questions.expected_answer: 02:30 local occurred twice when summer time ended, and the scheduler only blocks a second firing within 60 seconds.

required_questions.question: Why did the second run charge again?
required_questions.expected_answer: renews_on advances only at 05:00 in settle_renewals, and the Payrail charge has no idempotency key.

required_questions.question: Is anything else affected?
required_questions.expected_answer: send_dunning fired twice and sent 41 reminders twice.

required_questions.question: How do we refund safely?
required_questions.expected_answer: Find which customers support already refunded, which no file lists, for example from Payrail refund records, then refund the rest.

valid_alternatives.option: Idempotent charge_renewals per subscription and period
valid_alternatives.trade_off: Protects against any double run, not only the clock change, but does not stop the second send_dunning.
valid_alternatives.primary_when: The team wants a guard at the charge itself, or other double runs are possible.

valid_alternatives.option: Scheduler fix that fires once per local slot
valid_alternatives.trade_off: Fixes every job at the source, but a later double run from another cause still double charges.
valid_alternatives.primary_when: The team wants one fix for all schedules.

valid_alternatives.trade_off: No repeated or skipped local hour, but the local run time shifts by one hour twice a year.
valid_alternatives.primary_when: The team accepts the seasonal shift of local run times.

closing_decision: One decision: approve the scheduler fix, with or without the idempotent charge guard, or a single follow-up such as how to find the manual refunds before the refund run.

understanding.problem: At the end of summer time the 02:30 local slot occurred twice and the scheduler fired charge_renewals twice.
understanding.breaks: 212 subscribers were charged twice and dunning reminders went out twice.
understanding.fix: Fire each local slot once in the scheduler, optionally make the charge idempotent, and refund the duplicates that support did not refund.
understanding.cost: A small scheduler change, an optional guard in charge_renewals, and a refund run that needs the list of manual refunds.
